# External current-fact evidence (new18 §104)

Every externally mutable platform claim, with its primary source, the date it was checked,
and the factual conclusion drawn. Primary sources only; concise summaries only — no vendor
documentation is reproduced here.

**What makes a claim externally mutable:** its truth lives on somebody else's server. A
support class, a primitive's state, and a submission's status can all become false without
anything in this repository changing. That is why `distribution-watch.yml` fetches the
`watch source` column weekly and fails the job when a fact moves, and why the
`checked-at` date below is the date of the SSOT edit that recorded the fact rather than the
date this file was generated.

Release 1.8.0. 31 claims across 18 hosts.

Every claim below carries a recorded factual conclusion.

Audited 2026-08-27. ClawHub hosts exactly three surfaces: Skills (a folder carrying `SKILL.md`), code plugins, and bundle plugins. It hosts no MCP servers, so the obvious reading of this row — publish the MCP server — has no target. But we already ship `skills/secure-agent-install/SKILL.md`, and `clawhub skill publish <path>` takes precisely that, with `--dry-run` first, so no new artifact would be needed. What stops it: publishing a skill to ClawHub releases it under `MIT-0`, and this repository is Apache-2.0. MIT-0 drops the attribution requirement and carries no patent grant, so the act would relicense a shipped artifact on strictly weaker terms than the repo it came from. That is an owner's decision about intellectual property, not an engineering step, and it cannot be inferred from the instruction to submit to shelves — so it is recorded here rather than performed. It also needs `clawhub login` (browser OAuth, `--device`, or a `clh_` token), which is an account only the owner has. Unblocking condition, stated so nobody re-audits: the owner accepts MIT-0 for that one skill directory, or ClawHub gains a per-skill licence field. |

Direct path/repo/URL installs are deprecated with a warning that only `plugin@marketplace` installs will be supported, which makes this PR the eventual only supported route rather than a nicety. There is no submission here at all: the gallery automatically indexes public repositories and the docs say in as many words that you need not submit an issue or email anyone. Three conditions, quoted from the releasing guide: the extension is hosted in a public GitHub repository; the repository carries the `gemini-cli-extension` topic, which is what the crawler uses to find new extensions; and `gemini-extension.json` sits in the absolute root of the repository or the release archive. Crawling is daily and listing is conditional on passing validation. No git tag or release is required — `migratedTo` is the only transition that needs one. So the first condition already holds, the third is an artifact this repository does not yet have, and the second is a one-call metadata change. Ordering matters and is the reason this is not done: adding the topic first invites a daily crawler to validate a repository with no manifest in it, and a listing that depends on passing validation should not first be observed failing it. Manifest before topic. |

## Candidate feeds

§85 watches these for NEW PLATFORM CANDIDATES only. A feed may never promote a host, add an
extractor, or claim support — §86 permits recording candidate evidence and nothing more.

| feed | vendor | role | primary source | conclusion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DeepSeek official curated agent lists | DeepSeek | NEW_CANDIDATE_FEED_ONLY | https://github.com/deepseek-ai/awesome-deepseek-agent | §85 lists this as NEW-CANDIDATE FEED ONLY. Watched to notice a harness CallLint does not yet track; it is never evidence about an existing host's support class. Prior evaluation (artifacts/harness-distribution/native/manifest.json) found the list collects harness integration guides rather than MCP tools, so CallLint does not fit its scope -- recorded as candidate evidence per §86, with no submission made. |
| Model Context Protocol -- example clients | Model Context Protocol | NEW_CANDIDATE_FEED_ONLY | https://modelcontextprotocol.io/examples | The protocol's own enumeration of MCP clients, and the highest-authority place a harness CallLint does not track would first appear. Verified 2026-08-22: HTTP 200, and the page body names clients (46 'client', 26 'cursor', 24 'Claude', 14 'host') rather than only tools -- the reason it qualifies as a harness feed at all. A FEED, not a host source: it is authority over what MCP clients EXIST, never over CallLint's support class for one, so it cannot live in `hosts`. Distinct from `officialMcpRegistry`, which is where CallLint's own server is PUBLISHED; this is where other people's harnesses are listed. |
| PulseMCP client directory | PulseMCP | NEW_CANDIDATE_FEED_ONLY | https://www.pulsemcp.com/clients | A third-party directory, included because breadth is the point of a candidate feed: it lists harnesses before a vendor documents MCP support, which is the window in which a candidate is worth noticing. Verified 2026-08-22: HTTP 200, body enumerates clients including VS Code, Cursor and Cline. NOT AN AUTHORITY, and the boundary matters more here than for a first-party feed -- if this directory claims a harness supports something, that claim has zero standing over `supportClass`, and §86 permits recording the candidate's existence and nothing else. Admission still requires human review and enters as DEFERRED or DISCOVERY_ONLY; NATIVE additionally requires a bootstrapped extractor, which HD-01 enforces independently of anything a directory says. |
